mathprobvault.com
A web application (Next.js, Docker) that maintains a single LaTeX-format database of mathematics problems. It serves two purposes: assembling tests and exams from a problem bank with automatic LaTeX generation, and archiving my own worked solutions to exercises from classical textbooks such as Axler’s Linear Algebra Done Right and Measure, Integration & Real Analysis and Grimmett & Stirzaker’s Probability and Random Processes, etc.
Visit mathprobvault.com →

title: About me
text:
I am a data analyst and a lecturer in mathematics. Since 2019 I have taught at the university level while working in parallel in retail analytics; my background is in probability theory.
I studied at the Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics of Lomonosov Moscow State University (2013–2019), Department of Probability Theory. My diploma thesis, Martingale couplings with prescribed properties and the Skorokhod embedding problem, was written under the supervision of Alexander Gushchin.
Since 2019 I have taught continuously at the university level while working in parallel as a data analyst. My interests span measure-theoretic probability, martingales and optimal transport, sequential analysis, and the design of interactive mathematical visualisations for teaching.

title: About me
text:
Research
My thesis develops the machinery of integrated distribution and quantile functions and applies it in three directions: a short alternative proof of the martingale convergence theorem and of Prokhorov’s theorem via uniform convergence of integrated quantile functions; an explicit martingale coupling minimising the martingale Wasserstein distance between two one-dimensional distributions, with the sharp constant in the inequality \(MW_1(\mu,\nu) \le 2\,W_1(\mu,\nu)\); and an explicit embedding of this coupling into Brownian motion by two constructed stopping times, as a special case of the Skorokhod embedding problem.
This line of work continued after graduation in joint work with Alexander Gushchin:

Gushchin, A. A. and Nedoshivin, M. A. (2022). On Perkins’ construction in the Skorokhod embedding problem. Talk at the 7th International Conference on Stochastic Methods (ICSM-7), Divnomorskoe, Russia. Abstract published in Theory of Probability and Its Applications, 67(4), 2023, pp. 662–663. DOI: 10.1137/S0040585X97T991210

title: About me
text:
Applied work
Since 2019 I have worked as a data analyst for the Azbuka Vkusa retail chain (from 2022 through its subsidiary AV Infotech). My day-to-day work centres on demand forecasting — including perishable categories and network-wide forecasts for the New Year peak season — seasonality and trend decomposition using Fourier analysis, and inventory data reconciliation. Alongside this, I’ve led a number of self-directed analytics and data-engineering projects:

On-shelf availability detection — a daily pilot comparing three independent detectors (a method-of-moments heuristic, a CUSUM detector in T-SQL window functions, and Bayesian online changepoint detection in Python) to flag items that are in stock on paper but have stopped selling.
Optimal order / replenishment policies for perishables — a Monte Carlo simulator comparing the current auto-ordering logic against alternative replenishment policies, balancing availability against write-offs.
Product classifier refinement and substitution analysis — merging item classifiers from source systems and measuring which product attributes shoppers actually look for when a substitute is needed.
Censored demand reconstruction — an EM-based prototype recovering true demand for SKUs whose sales are capped by stockouts.
Store clustering — grouping stores by shelf capacity and demand profile to inform assortment planning.
Geodata and location potential modelling — combining OpenStreetMap, routing, and population data to model revenue potential for new store locations.
OCR/MDM extraction — a working prototype that extracts structured product attributes (name, brand, weight, barcode, etc.) from label photos using vision-LLMs.
Personalised recommendations — a product concept and business case for a recommendation feature, not yet a built system.
Temperature-demand elasticity and a public holiday calendar ETL used as a shared input across forecasting projects.

Tools: T-SQL (SQL Server), Python, Quarto, JavaScript (D3.js, Plotly.js, Canvas), Next.js/React, Docker, LaTeX.
